To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

c-Myc expression is necessary for induction by LTAg of DNA synthesis in serum-starved cells, that LTAg can prevent c-Myc-mediated apoptosis, and that LTAg can do so by its interaction with the tumor suppressor protein p53.

the ability of simian virus 4 large tumor antigen to induce DNA synthesis in quiecent 3T1-L1 fibroblasts is mediated by the c-myc proto-oncogene and that c-myc expression is sufficient to cause programmed cell death in quiescent L1 cells, but that the large tumor antigen can prevent this apoptosis.
LTAg induces c-myc expression in L1 cells and that c-Myc is essential for LTAg-induced DNA replication and that LTAg prevents c-Myc induced apoptosis in serum-starred L1 cells by binding to p53.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of LTAg-induced DNA replication in quiescent cells.
the role of c-Myc and p53 in LTAg-induced cell cycle progression.
the mechanisms that control the expression of the c-myc protooncogene and its role in the regulation of cellular proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-Myc is required for DNA synthesis in quasiescent L1 cells expressing LTAg, but LTAg-K1 is unable to induce DNA synthesis due to a defect in p53 interaction.
c-Myc and LTAg are both required for induction of DNA replication in quiescent cells and that LTAg prevents apoptosis induced by c-Myc in serum-starved cells by binding of p53.
c-Myc is required for LTAg-induced DNA replication in serum-starved mouse fibroblastic cells, but that the LTAg-p53 interaction is required to prevent c-MYC-induced apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LTAg can induce DNA synthesis in quasiescent cells by two distinct mechanisms.
LTAg can induce DNA synthesis and c-Myc can induce apoptosis.
LTAg induces cellular DNA synthesis by a two-step mechanism involving binding of LTAg to pRb, leading to activation of c-Myc, and binding to p53, leading to inactivation of c-Myc-induced cell death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the c-Myc and pRb pathways are both important for LTAg-induced DNA replication in L1 cells and that LTAg can prevent c-Myc-mediated cell death.
c-myc is a necessary and sufficient factor for LTAg-induced DNA replication in quiescent cells.
c-Myc is a key regulator of LTAg-induced DNA replication in quiescent L1 cells.
